goal.text: The wearer is doing a final walk-through of the flat and wants a running, ordered tally of everything she has opened and shut on the way round.

turns.text: I want to walk the whole flat before we hand the keys back. What did I just do at that cupboard?

trigger.detail: user opens the walkthrough

expected_answer.text: You held the door open with one hand, lifted out a food pack with the other, looked it over while you talked, then put it back and shut the cupboard.

turns.text: Anything else come out of there while I had it open?

trigger.detail: gaze leaves the wall and settles on the cabinet she is closing

expected_answer.text: No. That was the only item you lifted out, and it went straight back onto the same shelf.

turns.text: Two more rooms since — have I opened anything, or just looked?

trigger.detail: arrives at the bathroom sink and reaches for the drawer

expected_answer.text: Just looked, until now. You walked the laundry room, leaned in at the bathroom doorway, then came in and put a hand on the vanity drawer.

turns.text: oh — by the way, was there a machine back in that first room?

trigger.detail: the washer-dryer stack leaves frame as she turns toward the bathroom

expected_answer.text: Yes, a stacked washer and dryer, on your left as you stepped in. It dropped out of view about seven seconds later.

turns.text: Back to that drawer. Did I close it, and with which hand?

trigger.detail: drawer shut and she leaves the bathroom

expected_answer.text: You did, with both hands. You opened it one-handed and needed two to push it shut again.

turns.text: mm-hm — actually, hold that. What did I just do to the bin?

trigger.detail: no new trigger; the user simply keeps the thread running

expected_answer.text: You leaned over it, flipped the lid open and closed it again with both hands, then stood up and pushed the door.

turns.text: wait — did I leave the curtain open back there?

trigger.detail: user worries about something left undone

expected_answer.text: No, you opened it and closed it again in one go, and it was your left hand both times.

turns.text: And so far, how many things have I opened and shut?

trigger.detail: walks out of the closet, hands free

expected_answer.text: Four: the kitchen cupboard, the bathroom drawer, the bin lid and the curtain.

turns.text: Make that five — I just did another one. What was it?

trigger.detail: hallway unit opened and closed, she turns away

expected_answer.text: The cupboard built into the hallway wall. You opened it and closed it again with your left hand, and took nothing out.

turns.text: um, hang on — that's twice I've touched a frame. Where first?

trigger.detail: user follows up on a repeated habit rather than a new event

expected_answer.text: On the bedroom door as you walked out of it, about ten seconds before you reached the hallway cupboard.

turns.text: Which hand did I use that time?

trigger.detail: user narrows the previous answer

expected_answer.text: Your right that time; the one just now was your left.

turns.text: Right — add this to the tally. What did I just take the lid off?

trigger.detail: cover goes back on and the container is set down

expected_answer.text: A box you picked up from the cabinet top in the living area. You took the cover off, put it straight back on, and set it down where it was.

turns.text: sorry, quick one — before that, I poked at something. What?

trigger.detail: user reaches back past the current action

expected_answer.text: Two things on the wall shelf: the potted plant first, then an ornament beside it, which you touched with your right hand.

turns.text: Can I still see it from where I am?

trigger.detail: the pot on the shelf drops out of frame as she turns

expected_answer.text: No. It went out of frame a couple of seconds ago as you turned into the dining area.

turns.text: Okay, and this desk — how many of these have I pulled open?

trigger.detail: second drawer closed, she moves to the lower door

expected_answer.text: Two drawers, one with each hand, and then the little door beside them. Everything you opened here you also closed.

turns.text: mm— sorry, one more thing on that desk: was there anything switched on?

trigger.detail: user keeps the desk thread alive while walking off

expected_answer.text: There was a monitor there, in view the whole time you stood at it. It left the shot when you turned away.

turns.text: hold on — where was the last mirror I went past?

trigger.detail: focus leaves the unit behind her for the shelving in the living area

expected_answer.text: In the dining area, on your left as you walked in; you went past it about half a minute ago.

turns.text: no, I mean — what's on that shelf I keep looking at?

trigger.detail: user repairs their own previous question

expected_answer.text: Decorations along the hanging shelf in the living area. You stopped by the chair to look, then pointed them out to your colleague.

turns.text: What did I just slide out and hold up to my nose?

trigger.detail: the tray comes out and she smells it

expected_answer.text: The salt tray from the humidifier. You pulled it out with one hand, smelled it, then slid it back in.

turns.text: And is it seated properly now?

trigger.detail: user checks the state of the thing just discussed

expected_answer.text: Yes. You pushed it home with your right hand and then leaned over the unit again.

turns.text: I've been breaking up that salt bed for ages. What have I turned up?

trigger.detail: the hammer goes down and she reaches into the salt

expected_answer.text: Two pieces so far: a stone you lifted out with your left hand, and then a small figure beside it. You put both back down.

turns.text: And what have I been using on it?

trigger.detail: user asks about the instrument rather than the result

expected_answer.text: A hammer, held in your right hand. You set it down each time you spotted something, then picked it up again.

turns.text: So that's the lot — give me the running list back, in order.

trigger.detail: focus leaves the counter unit for the far wall as she drinks

expected_answer.text: The ones we counted, in order: the kitchen cupboard, the bathroom drawer, the bin, the curtain, the hallway cupboard, the box, and the two drawers and door at the desk.

turns.text: And this one in my hand, where did I pick it up?

trigger.detail: user asks about the object they are holding

expected_answer.text: Off the table as you came through into the kitchen, a few seconds before you stopped at the counter.

turns.text: Perfect. That's the whole place done.

trigger.detail: user closes the exchange

expected_answer.text: Good. Shout if you want the list again.
